subject: physics
question_text: How can systematic errors be minimised or eliminated?

verification.note: Unit 2 has NO Short Answer or Long Answer section in EITHER source book — the Fastrack (pp.4-5) and the TSBIE Basic Learning Material (pp.2-3) both list Very Short Answer questions only. So every Unit 2 card is a 2-mark VSAQ and no 8-mark form is invented. The 1+1 mark split is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it; the question itself is sourced, not invented.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Why they need removing
lines: A systematic error shifts every reading in the
same direction, so taking more readings and
steps.why: Averaging cancels errors that change sign. A systematic error never changes sign, so the average carries the same shift as every single reading.
common_mistakes: Saying they are removed by taking many readings. That reduces random errors, not systematic ones.

recall.must_convey: That a systematic error shifts every reading the same way, so averaging cannot remove it.

steps.memory_tip: Averaging kills random errors only. A systematic error survives the average.
steps.margin_note: Say why first. It makes the remedies make sense.

steps.label: The remedies

lines.text: Improve the technique and the instrument

lines: Correct for a known zero error, choose a
better instrument, and remove personal bias
steps.why: Each remedy attacks the source rather than the readings: a zero error is corrected, a coarse instrument is replaced, an observer bias is trained out.
common_mistakes: Giving only one remedy when the question says "minimised or eliminated".

recall.must_convey: That they are reduced by better technique, better instruments, correcting zero error and removing personal bias.

steps.memory_tip: Fix the SOURCE: zero error, instrument, observer. Not the arithmetic.
steps.margin_note: Three short remedies are plenty at 2 marks.

insider_note: Both books ask this. Systematic errors are the ones averaging cannot remove — say that, then list the remedies.
